subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: During gel electrophoresis of DNA fragments, the fragments move towards the anode (positive electrode) because:
options: The phosphate groups give DNA an overall negative charge
DNA carries an overall positive charge
Larger fragments are repelled by the gel
questions.explain: The phosphate backbone gives DNA a net negative charge, so fragments migrate towards the positive anode.

questions.q: A tRNA anticodon is 5'-UAC-3'. The mRNA codon it pairs with is:
questions.explain: Antiparallel complementary base pairing of anticodon 5'-UAC-3' gives codon 5'-GUA-3'.

questions.q: Activated nucleotides used in DNA replication carry two extra phosphate groups. The breaking of these bonds:
options: Releases energy that drives the condensation reaction joining nucleotides
Removes errors from the new strand
questions.explain: Hydrolysis of the two additional phosphates releases energy that powers phosphodiester bond formation.

questions.q: Allopatric speciation occurs when populations are reproductively isolated by:
options: A change in mating season only
A behavioural difference within the same area
A geographical barrier such as a mountain or river
questions.explain: In allopatric speciation a physical/geographical barrier separates populations, allowing them to diverge.

questions.q: Red-green colour blindness is X-linked recessive. A carrier mother and an unaffected father have children. What proportion of their sons are expected to be colour blind?
questions.explain: Sons inherit one of the mother's two X chromosomes, so half receive the affected X and are colour blind.

questions.q: Genetic drift has the greatest effect on allele frequencies in:
options: Small populations, where chance events strongly affect allele frequencies
questions.explain: In small populations, random chance (drift) can cause large fluctuations in allele frequencies between generations.

questions.q: DNA replication is described as semi-conservative rather than conservative because experiments showed that after one round of replication in heavy then light isotopes, all DNA was:
options: A mixture of fully heavy and fully light molecules
Of intermediate density (one heavy strand, one light strand)
questions.explain: Meselson and Stahl found a single intermediate-density band after one generation, supporting semi-conservative replication.

questions.q: In the Hardy-Weinberg equations, q squared represents the frequency of:
questions.explain: q squared is the frequency of the homozygous recessive genotype, since q is the recessive allele frequency.

questions.q: A geneticist obtains a chi-squared value with a probability (p) of 0.30 that the deviation is due to chance. The correct conclusion is to:
options: Accept the null hypothesis as the deviation is not significant
questions.explain: As p is greater than 0.05, the deviation is not significant, so the null hypothesis is accepted.

questions.q: A dihybrid cross between two double heterozygotes shows a phenotypic ratio significantly different from 9:3:3:1. This deviation is best explained by:
options: Autosomal linkage between the two genes
questions.explain: Linkage keeps parental allele combinations together, distorting the expected independent-assortment 9:3:3:1 ratio.

questions.q: Decreased acetylation of histones (deacetylation) tends to:
options: Make chromatin more condensed and decrease transcription
questions.explain: Histone deacetylation increases positive charge, tightening DNA-histone binding and condensing chromatin to reduce transcription.

questions.q: In a chi-squared calculation, each term is found by:
questions.explain: Chi-squared sums (O - E) squared divided by E across all categories.

questions.q: The standard hierarchy of taxonomic ranks, from largest to smallest, is:
options: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom, Domain
Kingdom, Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Domain, Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Family, Order, Genus, Species
questions.explain: The accepted order is Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.q: In epistasis, when a recessive allele at one locus in the homozygous state prevents expression of a second gene, this is termed:
questions.explain: Recessive epistasis occurs when the homozygous recessive genotype at one locus masks the second gene's expression.

questions.q: Continuous variation (e.g. human height) is typically caused by:
options: Many genes acting together (polygenic) plus environmental influence
A single gene with two alleles
questions.explain: Continuous variation is polygenic, with many genes and the environment producing a range of phenotypes.

questions.q: The founder effect occurs when:
options: A small group establishes a new population carrying only a subset of the original gene pool
A large population is split equally by a barrier
questions.explain: A few founding individuals carry only part of the parent population's genetic variation, skewing allele frequencies in the new population.

questions.q: In prokaryotes, unlike eukaryotes, mRNA does not require splicing because:
questions.explain: Prokaryotic genes generally lack introns, so the mRNA is functional without splicing.

questions.q: Reproductive isolation is essential for speciation because it:
options: Prevents gene flow between diverging populations so they accumulate genetic differences
questions.explain: Without gene flow, populations diverge genetically until they can no longer interbreed, becoming separate species.

questions.q: The genetic code is described as 'degenerate'. This means that:
options: Most amino acids can be coded for by more than one codon
Some codons do not code for any amino acid
Each codon codes for more than one amino acid
questions.explain: Degeneracy means most amino acids are specified by more than one triplet codon.

questions.q: A person with blood group AB has the genotype:
questions.explain: Group AB results from codominant alleles IA and IB both being expressed.

questions.q: Human birth mass shows that very small and very large babies have higher mortality, while intermediate masses survive best. This illustrates:
questions.explain: Selection against both extremes in favour of the intermediate is stabilising selection.

questions.q: Crossing over between linked genes during meiosis produces:
options: Recombinant offspring with new allele combinations
questions.explain: Crossing over swaps alleles between homologous chromosomes, generating recombinant combinations among linked genes.

questions.q: Sympatric speciation differs from allopatric speciation because it occurs:
options: Only after a geographical barrier forms
Without geographical separation, e.g. by behavioural or temporal isolation
questions.explain: Sympatric speciation happens within the same geographical area through reproductive isolation mechanisms other than geography.

questions.q: In sex linkage, a characteristic feature of pedigrees for X-linked recessive traits is that:
options: Affected fathers always pass it to their sons
An affected father passes the allele to all his daughters but none of his sons
questions.explain: A father passes his single X to all daughters (making them carriers) but passes his Y, not his X, to sons.

questions.q: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to the 3' end of a strand. This explains why:
options: The lagging strand is synthesised discontinuously as Okazaki fragments
The leading strand is synthesised in fragments
Helicase is required to join the fragments
questions.explain: Because synthesis must run 5' to 3', the antiparallel lagging strand is built discontinuously as Okazaki fragments later joined by ligase.

questions.q: During transcription, which enzyme joins RNA nucleotides together to form pre-mRNA?
questions.explain: RNA polymerase catalyses the formation of phosphodiester bonds between RNA nucleotides during transcription.

questions.q: In a population, the frequency of the dominant allele (p) is 0.6. Assuming Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the frequency of heterozygotes is:
A high value of an index of diversity (e.g. Simpson's index) for a habitat indicates:
options: Few species and many individuals of one species
Many species each fairly evenly represented
questions.explain: A high diversity index reflects many species in relatively even proportions, indicating a more stable ecosystem.

questions.q: The Hardy-Weinberg principle predicts that allele and genotype frequencies remain constant only if:
options: The population is small with frequent migration
There is no mutation, no selection, no migration, random mating and a large population
questions.explain: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes a large population with no mutation, selection or migration and random mating.

questions.q: The site of translation in a eukaryotic cell is the:
questions.explain: Translation occurs at ribosomes, where mRNA codons are read to assemble a polypeptide.
